display_name: The Ordinance of the Hearth Crown

clergy.vestments: cream robes, bronze belts, and red half-capes clasped with house seals
clergy.holy_symbol: a crowned hearthfire within a ring

cosmology.opposing_view_detail: Chaotic powers are named ravening pretenders that mimic divinity only to unmake law, kinship, and harvest.
cosmology.notes: See §3.3 Alignment Cosmology Rules for the hard constraints governing this field.

pantheon.domains_summary: Aurenthar guards rightful rule, clear judgment, and the light that reveals hidden wrongs.

pantheon.holy_symbol: three wheat heads tied in white cord
pantheon.domains_summary: Brythea governs planting, birth, and the obligation to feed the needy in lean years.

pantheon.holy_symbol: a hammer over a square ember
pantheon.domains_summary: Caudren sanctifies lawful craft, sworn contracts, and the making of useful, enduring things.

pantheon.holy_symbol: a spear laid across a roadstone
pantheon.domains_summary: Selvor protects levies on campaign, guarded roads, and the fortune earned through prepared courage.

pantheon.holy_symbol: a crescent above an open tablet
pantheon.domains_summary: Merial oversees memory, lawful omens, and the patient study that prevents disaster.

flavor_text.one_line: A civic pantheon of judged light, sworn labor, and shared bread under rightful rule.
flavor_text.one_paragraph: The Ordinance teaches that the world is held together by sacred obligations: ruler to village, parent to child, host to guest, and rich to hungry. Its temples stand near granaries, courts, and mustering fields, insisting that law without mercy becomes tyranny and mercy without law becomes ruin. Chaotic powers are denounced as lying idols that promise freedom while scattering famine, fire, and betrayal.
flavor_text.creation_myth_summary: The gods kindled the first hearth at the dark center of the world, then ringed it with law so people could build villages instead of preying on one another.
flavor_text.moral_code_summary: Keep oaths, obey just authority, feed the helpless, pay fair measure, and resist Chaos wherever it breaks covenant, harvest, or peace.
